name: manual_1079e8
claim: Supersedes only claim (4) of lesson_e0ff7f2d6717 (the immutable-builder-via-structural-sharing synthesis for MiniGraph.add_node/add_edge). That change was reverted the same day it was made, after being checked against evidence rather than defended on its own terms: searched 8 independent real-world LangGraph sources (official API reference, official docs.langchain.com Graph API guide, 6 tutorials) for how StateGraph.add_node is actually called in practice. Every single one calls builder.add_node(...) as a bare statement in a loop or sequence, never builder = builder.add_node(...) -- zero exceptions found. Reproduced directly that an immutable MiniGraph silently discards every such call (builder._nodes stays empty, no error raised), which would have broken all 8 real examples if ported to this codebase. The correct resolution: MiniGraph reverted to mutable (add_node/add_edge mutate self and return self, matching real StateGraph's own documented Self-returning pattern), because a finding that satisfies an unlocated abstract "always create new objects" rule while silently breaking the project's own stated, higher-priority LangGraph-drop-in-compatibility goal (doc 57 section 17) is not a correct resolution of that finding. The compile()-boundary immutability claims from lessons 1-3 and 5 of lesson_e0ff7f2d6717 (the deep=True fix, the _run()/GraphObservation reconciliation, the R2.4 strengthening, and the merge-conflict-resolution mechanics) remain valid and unaffected by this correction -- only the MiniGraph-itself-immutable claim is retracted. Commit faf27d2c on orama-system's 2026-08-27-minigraph-final-reconciliation branch.

decisions.notes: Real code was reverted the same day it was written, after being checked against verified evidence and found to break the project's own stated priority goal -- this correction must be on record, not silently absorbed into the prior lesson.
